What I'm trying to say is that this film should not be shown at all before you deal with its admission into evidence, especially not in the context of having this as evidence to prove that Dragomir Milosevic took part in all of this, that the learned Prosecutor Stefan referred to. This really should not be presented now. It is for you to judge, but I have to object at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, let's hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I accept the comments from my learned colleague, but this is an opening statement, Your Honours, and this is not evidence. What I'm saying just comes out of my mouth and is an outline of what the Prosecution is to present. All these documents I have shown, the videos I intend to show, witness quotes I made, that's argument from my side. And only when we start the trial on Monday, evidence will be presented. So this is just for Your Honours to see what is coming, the video, this is not evidence, the video. Mr. Tapuskovic is perfectly fine to challenge the moment a witness is going to tender these video-clips. He can say it's whatever, it's not accurate, or it's not reliable, that's the time for him to challenge this video, but certainly not during the opening. It's not evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, I hear your argument, but the practice here is to allow some latitude in opening statements, which do not constitute evidence. Accordingly, the Prosecutor can show the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Perhaps if the lights could be dimmed in the courtroom so we can see it more clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, Prosecution is confident that once all the evidence is in, the Chamber will render the only verdict that is justified by the evidence presented and that the accused, Dragomir Milosevic, is guilty beyond reasonable doubt of all he counts of the amended indictment. Your Honours, this concludes the Prosecution's opening statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Waespi. Mr. Tapuskovic, my understanding is that you do not wish to make a statement now. May I have that confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I shall confirm that for you, and I believe that that is something that we will do only prior to our own case. Also, I can say to you straight away that Dragomir Milosevic, the accused, is not [Realtime transcript read in error "now"] going to avail himself of the right given to him by the Rules to perhaps state something on him on his own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. It still remains for me to inquire of you, Mr. Tapuskovic, what your position is on that second Prosecution 65 ter motion where the witness is scheduled to give evidence next week. Do you remember we discussed that yesterday? 92 ter motion, I should have said, and I think you had -- we discussed two, and the position is that the time for your response had not yet expired and the witnesses are scheduled to give evidence next week. In relation to one you said there was no difficulty, but I believe you indicated that you would let us know today what your position was in relation to the second.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we are talking about Witness Fortin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, in relation to Witness Fortin, I think Mr. Tapuskovic indicated his approval of the Prosecution's plan and you were meant to ask him about David Harland.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I said last time that I'm not opposed to having that witness heard at all. It was my understanding that he would be the first witness that is to be called on Monday, that is witness 56. Is that not right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, but the issue is that we have recently filed a motion to have his testimony in the Slobodan Milosevic case admitted, selected parts of it, admitted under 92 ter. So our examination-in-chief will be fairly brief, and if the Defence agrees and Your Honours rule so, it will be fairly brief. But if the motion is denied, you know, we have to lead him for a considerable length of time. That's the issue. Mr. Harland will come to testify Monday. The issue is whether the Prosecution is allowed to lead him via the Rule 92 ter -- 92 ter it's called, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honours, I think that last time -- well, obviously there is some misunderstanding here because I responded to the Trial Chamber straight away that I absolutely agree to that, to having that admitted according to 62 -- no, 92 ter. I don't know. Obviously this is some kind of misunderstanding. I agreed to that, so I really don't know now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tapuskovic. I should have relied on my own recollection which is consistent with what you just said just then. Very well. We are ready to start on Monday of next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh -- I would have a question -- I mean, it's not even procedural. It's more of a technical nature. You said very clearly last time that if we have documents or evidence that is longer than 100 pages, I believe, that in that case we have to submit everything that will be the subject of our cross-examination 72 hours in advance, yes. Now, working on the examination of this witness Harland, I have, for example, two documents. I have two matters, rather, that I would like to have admitted. One is the statement that he gave as far back as 1997 or 1998 that he was questioned on. I'm not going to have many questions on that, it's about 25 pages. But I have, for example, a document, an UNPROFOR report that is on the 92 -- no, 65 ter list, and that is 55 pages long. And now, from that document, I just have a few sentences that I wish to use. Now, since that is already among the material presented by the Prosecution, according to their rules that have to do with evidence, now if I want to bring in these two documents that have almost 100 pages, is it that I can do nothing about this, or is it that I can just introduce these two pages? I do apologise, but this new electronic system is quite a new thing to me as well. If I was to introduce these two documents, then I'm totally paralysed, you see.

utterances.text: Are you in a position to indicate now what are those pages to which you will make specific reference?
